01 / FIRST STEPS

Make Pulse yours

1. Learn the bottom tabs

Watch (pulse icon) is the live and upcoming hub. Rituals (shirt icon) organizes weekly viewing windows. Stories (stars icon) offers narrative feeds and explainers. Use a back arrow to leave a detail screen.

2. Open Settings with the gear

Expand Your Favorites to enable or disable sports, leagues and teams. Expand Networks to review viewing-network preferences; Sports Packs groups coverage preferences. If a list seems short, check your selected sports and favorites-only setting.

3. Set your spoiler preference

Hide scores in Daily Wrap affects displayed final scores in that wrap, not all headlines or live score cards elsewhere. Open the gear again to change it at any time.

Before you begin

Pulse helps you discover an event; a provider may require its own account, subscription or regional access. A Watch link opens an external service rather than playing video inside Pulse.

02 / LIVE DISCOVERY

Use Watch

1. Scan the Watch hub

Look at the Chaos pick and its accompanying strip, then scroll through Live Now, Up Next and recent results. A quiet feed can simply mean no eligible live fixtures are available.

2. Narrow ordinary schedules

Use sport or league chips and, where shown, Favorites only to focus the flat event lists. Those controls do not strictly limit Chaos Mode, which can surface a compelling game outside your favorites.

3. Open an event

Tap its card for status, score, time, matchup and available provider actions. Join Live is for an available live link; Starting soon may be disabled before kickoff; Watch Replay is dependent on a finished event and available replay.

A quick reset

The Shuffle control rebuilds the Chaos selection. It is not an activity-trigger setting or a promise that the list will change if the candidate pool is small.

03 / HOW CHAOS WORKS

Tension is contextual

Chaos ranks eligible events using favorites, anchor matchups, live status, start time, emotion and sport-aware tension. A close score is not the whole ranking. Without a live score, a live game starts at rank 1; a non-live event is rank 0.

SportWhen tension rises
Hockey / soccerAfter opening period/half: margin ≤1 = rank 3; margin 2 = rank 2. Opening P1 / 1H closeness is suppressed.
RugbyMargin ≤7 = 3; margin 8–14 = 2.
BasketballFinal minute, within 5 OR final 2 minutes, within 3 = 4. Final 2 minutes within 6 or endgame within 3 = 3. Other one-point margins = 2. Endgame includes Q4/OT or college second half.
RacingRace session = 3; sprint or qualifying = 2; other sessions = 1.
Cricket / otherCricket = 1; other sports: margin ≤1 = 3, margin 2 = 2.

For any live sport with score data, a status/period containing OT, overtime, extra, shootout or penalty adds 2 to that sport’s baseline rank, capped at 5. It does not replace the sport-specific rules above: basketball still has its own endgame thresholds and cricket normally starts at 1. The UI labels rank 2 Heating Up, 3 Tight Game, and 4+ High Drama; “High Tension” appears at rank ≥3.

Read the strip separately

The hero is the main Chaos pick. A promoted game can lead the secondary strip visually without replacing that hero.

04 / CHAOS ALERTS

Why slot 4 changes

Pulse compares the current and previous available live-score snapshots to detect activity. These internal signals inform the in-app Chaos Alert; they are not adjustable user triggers, push notifications or background monitoring.

SignalPointsImportant condition
Score change+40Live eligible non-tennis/cricket score increase; basketball only in final 2 min.
Overtime / extra time+35Hockey, soccer or rugby overtime-type status.
Late close game+20Sport-specific late/close criteria; see notes below.
Hockey power play / goal / goalie pulled+20 / +25 / +25“Power play start” signal checks an active man advantage, not a start transition; goal requires a score change.
Tennis match point / upset+35 / +30Match-point detail or game/set inference; upset from rank gap ≥5 with lower-ranked player leading.
Racing red flag / safety car / final laps+30 / +20 / +25Status data; final laps begin at ≥85% of total laps.

Late-close detection includes hockey third period ≤10 min with ≤1-goal margin; soccer second half ≤1; rugby second half ≤7; tennis tied/near-tied later sets; basketball endgame ≤2 min and ≤5 points. A missing feed signal cannot produce that detection.

Hypothetical, not a screen capture

Suppose the fourth selected game has activity 20. An unselected live hockey game gains a goal (+40) while a current man advantage is detected (+20), totaling 60. The code names this +20 signal “Power play start,” but checks current skater counts, not a transition from even strength. Because 60 is at least 15 above 20, the challenger may replace only slot 4. The first three selected slots stay stable; the promoted game can lead the secondary strip, not the hero.

05 / YOUR WEEKEND

Six fixed ritual windows

Tap Rituals on the bottom bar. Swipe its large cards, then tap a card to enter its guide. Each card presents a mood and a time window; the windows below are fixed in Pacific Time, not configurable reminders.

CardWeekly window (PT)How to use it
Family Game NightFriday 6–9 pmBegin the evening with a featured pick.
Friday Night ModeFriday 9 pm–midnightLook for later games and a relaxed follow-up.
Warm-UpSaturday 6 am–noonBrowse the early weekend slate.
Game DaySaturday 4–8 pmFollow the main Saturday window.
Extra TimeSaturday 8 pm–midnightCatch late-session events.
Coffee & ChillSunday 6 am–noonEase into Sunday’s first games.
Time zone note

Individual fixture timestamps may show in your device’s zone or as UTC in certain feeds. Do not read a UTC fixture time as a PT ritual-window boundary. Check the event detail before making plans.

06 / INSIDE A RITUAL

Read the guide

1. Enter from the Rituals card

The guide opens with the window description and automatically selected Featured game, if one is eligible. Tap the featured event for its matchup sheet and available viewing action.

2. Browse by purpose

Favorites gathers games involving followed teams; Catch Up offers recent finished events where available; More Games presents other candidates. The groups depend on available event data, so one can be empty.

3. Use the chips

Sport and league chips narrow the guide’s list. If a game disappears, return to All or clear the narrowed league/sport. These are list filters, not a way to adjust the fixed ritual window.

Featured versus list

The Featured choice is a single highlighted matchup. Choosing another featured event does not add or remove a favorite team and does not change your Serie A My Plan.

07 / FEATURED OVERRIDE

Change the featured game

1. Open a ritual guide

Tap one of the six Rituals cards, not a Watch card. Scroll beneath the Featured area to Favorites or More Games if necessary.

2. Tap the game you want

In the guide, tapping a candidate game opens its matchup modal instead of normal event navigation. Review the game and tap Set as Featured.

3. Confirm the new selection

Return to the guide: the chosen game appears in Featured with a MANUAL badge. The guide removes that game from the other lists to avoid showing the same event twice.

4. Return to automatic choice

Tap Reset to Auto by Featured or in the game modal. The ritual then uses its automatically chosen featured game again.

How long it lasts

Manual choice persists on this device, not as an account-wide edit. An unavailable/ended selection is not kept indefinitely; old manual selections expire after about six hours. No notification is sent when the pick changes.

09 / THE DAILY WRAP

Catch up without losing control

1. Open the Daily Wrap cover

Read the wrap’s vertically scrolling story feed. The visible date and available cards reflect the generated content; no particular league or result is guaranteed.

2. Listen or read

Use the speaker/narration control if offered and mute it when you prefer silent reading. Narration is an optional playback aid, not a substitute for the on-screen text.

3. Follow the evidence

A story may offer a highlight, replay, or View Matchup path. Open the relevant action to check the event/provider detail; external media availability can vary.

4. Hide final scores

Settings → Hide scores in Daily Wrap controls score display there. It does not scrub every outcome from story headlines or hide live scores throughout the app.

If a result seems old

Refresh Schedules checks fixture data; Rebuild Stories refreshes narrative content. They are separate controls.

10 / WHAT’S NEXT

Today is an action list

1. Open What to Watch Next

Tap the cover from Stories. The Today tab is the immediate event view and follows your device-local calendar day.

2. Pick a sport

Use Today’s sport chips to narrow event cards, then scroll for more. A missing sport or empty list may mean no matching event on that local day; clear chips before assuming the feed failed.

3. Read the full context

Tap an event card or its Read more action where offered to reach the matchup or a relevant explainer. The View my plan control opens the Serie A pilot, not a general reminder calendar.

Two clocks in one guide

Ritual windows are fixed PT. Today follows your device date; a specific event may appear with a UTC timestamp in source-facing material. Verify the displayed event time and its zone before you watch.

11 / WHAT’S NEXT

Look farther ahead

1. Switch tabs

Choose This Week for the near-term slate; This Month and Next Month for the larger schedule overview. If weekly snapshot data is unavailable, its tab may not appear.

2. Read the month view correctly

Month rows group leagues and tournaments and show date ranges and season phases. Finals may appear as separate informational rows. These summaries are not promises of a fixture for every day.

3. Move from overview to action

For an actual event, return to Today/Watch or open a related matchup. Use the relevant sport chip or schedule filter to reduce clutter rather than treating a month league row as a watch link.

Why weeks and months differ

The week and month sections depend on available snapshot data; the Today view uses events for the device-local day. An informational league phase may remain even when individual matches are not supplied.

12 / TRENDING

Read the story, then act

1. Tap Trending

The feed is made of timely narrative cards; swipe/scroll vertically to read more. Kind labels can include Playoff Push, Momentum, Player Movement, Upset Alert, Rivalry Game and Week Ahead.

2. Check time and impact

The elapsed-time cue tells you how recent a narrative is. Impact text can point toward a Watch event or Rituals context, but it is not a guaranteed live-alert subscription.

3. Open the longer item

Tap Read full story when present. Depending on the card, the longer article may include optional media and related upcoming events. Follow a related event to its matchup and provider options.

Keep your bearings

Narratives are generated from available source data. Time labels and topical headlines can become stale; use Rebuild Stories if needed, and confirm live information on the event card.

PLAYBOOK / 01

Hockey Family Tree

This reference lists NHL clubs with their AHL development partner and ECHL affiliate(s). Open Behind the Stories → Hockey Family Tree; scroll club by club rather than looking for a live game card.

How to read a club card

The NHL badge and team name anchor the card. Beneath it, the AHL row identifies the development partner; one or more ECHL rows may follow. “No affiliate” means the entry has no listed relationship in that tier, not that the NHL team does not exist.

Why it matters

Use a prospect’s organization to understand why an AHL or ECHL game might matter to NHL followers. Affiliations can change between seasons; use the article’s verification note as context and report a suspected outdated mapping through Settings.

Try it

Find a club you follow, read its AHL row, then compare its ECHL rows. Return to Stories and look for a related game in Watch; the reference itself is not a provider link.

PLAYBOOK / 02

Cycling Circuits

Open Behind the Stories → Cycling Circuits. Scroll through both sections; these are different kinds of stage racing.

Grand Tours — the Big Three

Giro d’Italia (May, pink jersey), Tour de France (July, yellow jersey), and Vuelta a España (August–September) each run about three weeks on the road. Look for cumulative standings as well as stage wins.

Epic Series — Mountain Bike Stage Racing

Pairs race multiple stages together; Cape Epic (March), 4Islands Epic (April), Andorra Epic Pyrenees (July), Swiss Epic (August), and Wines2Whales (November) are the article’s named events. Terrain and partner pacing matter; pairs risk a penalty if they finish too far apart.

When browsing Watch

A one-day cycling fixture is not necessarily a Grand Tour stage. Read the event’s series/session detail before assuming it corresponds to a playbook example.

PLAYBOOK / 03

Endurance Athletics

Open Behind the Stories → Endurance Athletics and scroll through all five circuits, not only the opening Marathon Majors list.

  • World Marathon Majors: Tokyo, Boston, London, Sydney, Berlin, Chicago and New York City; the article distinguishes the seven events from Abbott Six Star status for the six core majors.
  • Comrades Marathon: South African ultramarathon between Durban and Pietermaritzburg, alternating Up/Down routes, with a strict 12-hour cutoff and tiered medals.
  • Wanda Diamond League: track-and-field meets award event points toward a season Final; compare event disciplines, not only the meet name.
  • Golden Trail World Series: technical, shorter mountain/trail races; examples include Zegama-Aizkorri, Sierre-Zinal and a Grand Finale.
  • UTMB World Series: long ultra-trail events award Running Stones toward UTMB Mont-Blanc; distances and climbing are central to the story.
Interpret the card

A meet, marathon and ultra are not interchangeable. Read the circuit heading before following any related date or provider note.

PLAYBOOK / 04

Paddling 101

Open Behind the Stories → Paddling 101 and read its three parts: the races, the format, and what to watch for.

SA Big Three

Dusi (February, 120 km / three days) is known for portages; Berg River (July, 240 km / four days) tests weather and endurance; Fish River (October, 82 km / two days) is faster and technical with dam-fed rapids. A same-year sweep is an unofficial paddling triple crown.

How a canoe marathon works

K1 means singles, K2 doubles. Participants start in seeding batches. Rapids, flat water and overland boat carries share the course; cumulative time across days determines the leader, not only the final stage.

What to watch for

Watch water levels and release announcements, portage speed, and how early leaders pace themselves across successive days. The article names leading South African paddlers as context, not a guarantee of their entry.

PLAYBOOK / 05

Triple Crown 101

Open Behind the Stories → Triple Crown 101 to read the three sections: why the achievement matters, the three Classics, and race-card vocabulary.

Why the sweep is rare

Only three-year-old thoroughbreds can compete, so each horse has one chance. Winning three spring races in roughly five weeks tests pace, recovery and stamina.

The three Classics

Kentucky Derby (first Saturday in May, Churchill Downs, 1¼ miles); Preakness Stakes (third Saturday in May, Pimlico, 1 3/16 miles); Belmont Stakes (early June, traditionally Belmont Park, 1½ miles). Verify current venue and broadcast details before a given season.

How to read a race card

Post position is the starting gate; morning line is an estimated pre-race price, not final odds. A furlong is ⅛ mile. Exacta predicts first and second in order; trifecta predicts the first three in order.

PLAYBOOK / 06

Racing 101

Open Behind the Stories → Racing 101; read all three sections before comparing a race event with a qualifying session.

Formula 1 — the circuit pinnacle

Practice tunes a car, knockout qualifying sets the grid, sprint weekends add a shorter points race, and Sunday’s Grand Prix is the main contest. Watch tyres, pit windows and the drivers’/constructors’ standings. The article lists Monaco, Britain, Belgium, Italy, Singapore and Abu Dhabi as marquee rounds.

World Rally Championship

A rally spans days of timed special stages; a single car races against the clock with a co-driver reading pace notes. Monte Carlo, Safari Kenya, Finland, Acropolis Greece and Saudi Arabia illustrate how surfaces and weather change strategy.

How to follow a season

Compare F1 race/sprint points with WRC stage-rally, Sunday and Power Stage points. Teams have separate constructors/manufacturers stakes. The article’s broadcaster and schedule examples are contextual, not guaranteed current availability.

14 / SAVE AN INTENTION

My Plan · Serie A

1. Open My Plan

From Watch, tap View my plan; a link may also appear in What to Watch Next. This is a Serie A pilot, not a universal sports planner.

2. Add a match

Open an eligible Serie A fixture and choose Watch live or Highlights. These are the two viewing intentions, not stream reservations.

3. Manage the list

Switch between This week and Upcoming, apply the available team filter, and edit an intention or remove a match if plans change. If the page is empty, add a supported fixture first.

Storage and delivery

The plan stays local to this device; it does not sync. Pulse does not send reminders or notifications for this plan. A Highlights intention does not guarantee a clip or replay becomes available.

15 / WHEN THINGS LOOK WRONG

Refresh & troubleshoot

Schedules missing or a list is empty

Check connection, enabled sports/leagues, Favorites only and any sport/league chips. Clear filters, then open Settings → Refresh Data → Refresh Schedules. An empty eligible slate is possible.

Stories are stale

Settings → Refresh Data → Rebuild Stories requests fresh narratives. This is separate from Refresh Schedules; refreshing events does not itself rebuild story text. A Stories pull-to-refresh may also request a rebuild.

An error appears

Read the exact on-screen error and retry the specific action. If it persists, record the screen, time, feature and message for support. Do not assume every empty result is a network error or suppress an explicit error.

Watch or Replay fails

Open the provider, check that you are signed in and that your package, territory and rights include that stream. Replay/highlights can arrive later or may never be offered. Pulse does not control third-party playback.

Scores and alerts

Live scores depend on active data feeds and refreshes. An in-app Chaos Alert appears while Watch is active when promotion conditions are observed; no push/background alert or user trigger configuration is promised.

16 / KEEP IN MIND

Reference & boundaries

QuestionReliable answer
Is Chaos a strict favorite filter?No. Favorites and anchors affect ordering, but compelling eligible games outside a flat list filter may appear.
Can I change alert thresholds?No user-adjustable trigger controls are provided.
Does “Hide scores” mean spoiler-free?No. Daily Wrap scores can be hidden, but headlines can reveal outcomes and live screens still show scores.
Are fixture times all Pacific?No. Ritual windows are PT; event times may be device-local or shown as UTC in some sources.
Are the screenshots live?No. They are authentic phone-sized web-preview captures from September 29 PT / September 30 UTC, 2026. Timestamps and scores are illustrative snapshots.
Does the plan sync or notify me?No. The Serie A pilot is device-local and sends no reminders.

Coverage is limited by data feeds, supported leagues, rights and providers. “Available” in a card never guarantees access to every fixture, score, highlight or replay. The app is a discovery layer, not a streaming subscription.
